### Day 365: Revelation 21:22–27
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-365-revelation-21-2227.html
Passage: Revelation 21:22
Points:
- Traditional Jewish weddings include breaking a glass to remember that earthly joy remains incomplete without the temple and departed loved ones.
- In Christ, believers find these longings answered because all who trust Him will be present together at the Lamb's supper.
- No physical sanctuary exists in the New Jerusalem because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are themselves its temple.
- Because God is directly and visibly present, worship no longer depends on earthly representations or symbols.
- Believers can look forward to a restored future where all sorrow ceases and joy is made fully complete.

### The New Jerusalem
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-new-jerusalem
Passage: Revelation 21:15-16
Points:
- John’s vision of the New Jerusalem draws heavily on Ezekiel’s prophetic description of the restored temple.
- Identifying the holy city as the bride demonstrates that John is describing the church triumphant rather than an ordinary earthly city.
- The equal dimensions of the city form a cube, deliberately echoing the Holy of Holies from the Old Testament temple.
- This imagery shows that God's redeemed people will live in His unhindered presence with all separation removed.
- Believers are urged to pursue holiness now in the Spirit while waiting for Christ to bring His work to completion.
